_README: Solar London CLIENT FACT SHEET - TEMPLATE, awaiting Raymon.
Per AGENTS.md section 7, every client has clients/<client>/facts.json and it is the single
source of truth for names, numbers, currency, percentages, dates and codes. Every document and
email must preserve each fact verbatim.
WHAT scripts/verify_document.py ACTUALLY DOES, AND WHAT IT CANNOT DO:
IT DOES  - for a PDF it extracts, check that every string in `must_appear` is present and every
string in `must_not_contain` is absent, in whitespace-normalised text.
IT CANNOT - read an HTML file. It parses bytes with pypdf, so the v1 quote output (an HTML
email) must be rendered to a PDF repo-side before the guard applies.
IT CANNOT - see anything outside these two keys. Every other key in this file is for humans
and agents; the script ignores them.
IT CANNOT - know the catalog. It cannot tell whether a figure on a quote came from the
catalog. A WRONG number passes it as long as it is not on the blocklist.
IT CANNOT - know the business. QA PROVED THIS: a PDF rebuilt from the old marketing copy
PASSES the guard. That is why a second check exists (see below).
IT CANNOT - match words, only substrings. 'CRO' also matches inside any word containing those
three letters, and 'null' matches inside 'nullable'. Over-broad entries cause false
failures, so risky entries are flagged in the note below.
THE GUARD IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. The check that actually catches wrong-business
content is clients/solar-london/build-spec/check_quote_content.py, which is DERIVED from
catalog.json and from the workflow export rather than from a hand-written list. Run BOTH:
CHECK 1  (fact sheet, placeholder and blocklist guard):
Render the quote repo-side to a PDF, then from the REPO ROOT:
python scripts/verify_document.py clients/solar-london/facts.json (Resolve-Path '<pdf>').Path
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'fact check FAILED - stage blocked' }
NEVER pass a literal glob such as clients/solar-london/pdfs/*.pdf. PowerShell does not expand
a wildcard for a native executable, the script receives the literal string, reports 'file not
found', and exits 1 ON A CORRECT FILE. Resolve the path in the shell first.
NEVER invoke it with fewer than two arguments. With none it prints its usage docstring and
exits 2 without performing a single check. Exit code 2 is not a pass.
For several files:
Get-ChildItem '<render dir>' -Filter *.pdf | ForEach-Object {
python scripts/verify_document.py clients/solar-london/facts.json $_.FullName }
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'fact check FAILED - stage blocked' }
Check $LASTEXITCODE explicitly. A printed 'ALL PASS' without an exit-code check is not a gate.
CHECK 2  (catalog and business-content guard - the one that catches the wrong business):
python clients/solar-london/build-spec/check_quote_content.py `
--catalog clients/solar-london/catalog.json `
--facts   clients/solar-london/facts.json `
--quote   <rendered quote text or html> `
--ledger  <price-ledger.json emitted by Build Quote Document> `
--export  <text-agent export> `
--expect-nodes 44
WHEN FILLING:
1. Copy this file to clients/solar-london/facts.json and fill it from Raymon's written answers only.
2. Add to `must_appear` ONLY strings Raymon has actually confirmed. Do not add a price to
`must_appear` until he gives that price in writing. An unconfirmed string in `must_appear`
fails every document and teaches the team to pad the list.
3. Leave `must_not_contain` populated. It is the anti-hallucination guard, not filler.
4. Re-run BOTH checks after every quote-document change.
5. Fill nothing from a reference site, a competitor, or a guess. An unknown fact stays "TBD".
must_appear_note: One confirmed fact exists so far. Everything else is genuinely unknown, and an unknown fact must never be guessed into a document. The fact sheet guards placeholders and a small blocklist; it does NOT guard that the right business is on the page, and it does NOT guard that a number came from the catalog. That is check_2's job.
must_not_contain_note: The [YOUR_*] and YOUR_GOOGLE_SHEET_* entries are literal placeholders the old quote workflow
shipped to customers. Their reappearance is a regression and must fail the stage.
'JR Marketing Agency', 'Social Media Marketing', 'CRO', 'Website Build' and 'SEO' came from the
old marketing-agency catalog. They are not Solar London services. Raymon's decision was that the
business is solar, so these are forbidden everywhere.
'TBD' is the load-bearing pricing sentinel. A delivered document must NEVER contain it. If it
does, an unresolved price leaked into a customer-facing document, which is the exact failure this
whole system is designed to prevent. Note this is a useful check while prices are still "TBD":
if a document containing 'TBD' can be produced at all, the abort path has a hole.
'recipient@example.com' was the hardcoded recipient in the old Gmail node.
SUBSTRING CAVEAT, confirmed by reading the script: it does substring matching, not word matching.
'CRO' also matches inside any word containing those three letters and 'null' matches inside
'nullable'. A zero-valued price is NOT in this list on purpose - a legitimate line total can
be zero and a false failure teaches the team to ignore the guard. The real defence against a zero
is that the pricing code aborts before a document is built, not that a blocklist catches it.
If a rendered document fails on one of these because of a substring collision, fix the ENTRY
or the CONTENT deliberately. Never delete an entry just to make the check green.

business.social_proof_note: The live persona cites a specific volume of five-star reviews. Confirm it is current and permitted on a client-facing quote before it appears on any document. "TBD" means the line is omitted, not guessed.
business.booking_url_note: Confirmed in the live persona prompt. A real booking link, not a placeholder - but it is a URL, not a price, and it is never to be treated as one.

persona.voice: British, casual, 30-year-old human, short messages, a few sentences, occasional spelling or grammar slip, never American, never emoji, never a long dash
persona.handoff_line_literal: let me check that with my manager
persona.handoff_line_provenance: Verbatim substring of this line in the live AI Conversation Agent systemMessage, read from the export dated 2026-09-26:
persona.handoff_line_source_sentence: IMPORTANT: If the requested information from the customer is not found you MUST check the Vector Datastore. If it is still not found you MUST tell the user something like: "let me check that with my manager".
persona.handoff_line_note: The literal in the quote sub-workflow is EXACTLY that substring and nothing more. An earlier draft appended a clause to it while still claiming to quote the persona, which is an unverifiable attribution. If a longer sentence is ever wanted it goes in a SEPARATE field, lead_line_continuation, which is never presented as coming from the persona. It is a literal in the workflow, not model output, so it matches Amy's voice by construction and cannot be hallucinated.

pricing.currency_note: GBP, stated once in spec section 2. It is not derived from any decision number; decision 4 was delivery by email. QA flagged the earlier citation of decision 4 as the currency decision and it was wrong.
pricing.source_quote_verbatim: it depends on what the person pick it a solar panel let say it about 6k pounds
pricing.source_quote_provenance: Raymon, in conversation, 2026-09-26. This is the ONLY price datum that exists.
pricing.source_quote_note: Deliberately null. The sentence is ambiguous in at least four ways: per panel or per install; VAT-inclusive or plus VAT; a real list price or a conversational illustration; home or commercial. It is recorded as the provenance of an open question and must NEVER be parsed into a price, used as a default, or used to bound a future Raymon-supplied value.
pricing.tbd_rule: Every price-bearing catalog field is the literal string "TBD" until Raymon supplies a value in writing. Money fields are strings on purpose; the pricing Code node parses them with /^\d{1,9}(\.\d{1,2})?$/ and treats any non-match as UNRESOLVED, which ABORTS the quote.
pricing.tbd_is_a_shipping_state: NOT a blocker. The system is complete and safe with every price at "TBD": the matcher runs, the strict price parse rejects "TBD", the quote aborts with needs_human true, the row is written with status blocked_tbd, and NO EMAIL IS SENT. The moment a real figure is written into unit_price and catalog_checksum is recomputed, the same graph quotes and emails. No code change, no node change, no re-wiring. The Builder must not treat "TBD" as a reason to stub, defer, or leave a node unwired.
pricing.fail_loud_rule: AGENTS.md section 9.7. An unresolved price aborts the quote and returns the pre-written handoff line. Never a partial quote, never a zero, never a range, never a model-invented number. A blocked email never means a silent lead - the handoff reply still goes out on the normal chat path, which this project does not touch.
pricing.unit_size_rule: unit_size is NOT a money field and is not parsed with the money regex. It is an integer count of WATTS matching /^[1-9][0-9]{1,4}$/ and requires unit_size_unit "W". A catalog value written for a kilowatt-scale system therefore FAILS validation and aborts, rather than silently pricing a three-kilowatt array as three watts. v1 supports watts only; converting kW to W is arithmetic Raymon has not authorised.
pricing.quantity_rule: quantity is a model-supplied STRING, validated as /^[1-9][0-9]{0,2}$/ then bounded by catalog policy.quantity.min and policy.quantity.max. It is REFUSED, never repaired and never defaulted. There is no fallback quantity anywhere in the build. While policy.quantity.max is "TBD" the effective cap equals the floor, so a multi-unit request is refused rather than priced on an unconfirmed bound.
pricing.price_basis_note: Is a quote a fixed price or a site-survey estimate? This changes document wording, not just a catalog line. If it is an estimate, terms_line is not optional.

email.sender_email_note: The Gmail node's From address. While "TBD" the run aborts with status blocked_tbd, failure_reason catalog_sender_email_tbd, and sends nothing. This must be an address on Solar London's own domain, controlled by Raymon long-term - a quote from a personal mailbox is a brand defect. See open question Q29.
email.delivery_method_decision: DECIDED, not open. The quote is sent by the stock n8n gmail node using a gmail OAuth2 credential Raymon creates on the instance from values already in the gitignored .env. See spec section 6.
email.delivery_method_why_not_ghl: The GHL private integration token Raymon supplied could not be validated - GHL returns an identical empty 404 for a valid token and an invalid token on every path tried. Building on an unvalidated credential against an API that fails indistinguishably is the silent-failure class this spec exists to eliminate. The Get a contact node that would have used it has no credential, no resource parameters, and is absent from the connections object entirely. NO node in this build calls the GoHighLevel API. GHL remains the lead entry point and the outbound chat path.
email.gmail_credential_rule: NO CREDENTIAL VALUE IS EVER WRITTEN INTO THIS FILE, into any spec, into any node, into any workflow export, into the build report, or into any committed file. Only the env var NAMES are recorded here. Raymon reads the values from the gitignored .env and types them into the n8n UI. GMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN exists in .env and is deliberately NOT used: access tokens are short-lived and the refresh token supersedes them.
email.gmail_credential_record_in_report: Record only the credential NAME, the connected account address, the scopes granted, and the date.
email.quote_email_webhook_url_note: null because it is NOT USED. A GHL outbound email webhook is documented as an explicit NOT-BUILT alternative in spec section 6.7, in case Raymon later wants the quote to land in the GHL conversation thread. If he ever chooses it, a new GHL automation is needed and a new trigger gets a NEW uuid - the three existing triggers on that location are WhatsApp/SMS and must not be reused.
email.recipient_rule: ONE rule, not three. email is REQUIRED. Missing, empty, or failing /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/ aborts the run with status bad_input and sends NOTHING. This matters more under the gmail node than it did under GHL: the address IS the delivery target, so this validation is the only thing standing between a transcription error and a customer's quote reaching a stranger's inbox. The quote is not emailed and the customer is not quoted.
email.body_email_path_note: UNVERIFIED. The live text agent references body.first_name, body['Message Aggregator'], body.contact_id and body.customData['AI Type']. It references body.email NOWHERE. Stage S3 must capture one real form fill and record the exact field path. Do not guess a path. Do not fall back to asking the customer for their address in chat - the systemMessage forbids it, and a chat-typed address is the hallucination this design exists to prevent.
email.pdf_attachment_route_note: v1 sends the quote as a styled HTML email body and produces NO attachment. This removes the unverified htmlcsstopdf community package, a Supabase Storage bucket that does not exist, and a signed-URL policy that would have to be invented. The PDF tail is v1.1, documented with its own complete node list in spec section 17.1 and marked NOT BUILT. Never a public bucket if it is ever added.
email.supabase_storage_policy: time-limited signed URL - never public read

data_store.quote_table_location: Supabase. NOT the Postgres database that holds Launchops_chat_memory.
data_store.quote_table_why_supabase: Three reasons. It removes the parameter-binding problem entirely - v1.0 specified SQL with a positional placeholder that n8n's Postgres node does not implement, and the only offered fallback was raw string interpolation, which is an injection path. Supabase is reached over PostgREST, which takes JSON, so no SQL text with a variable in it exists anywhere in this build. The quote data is per-lead and timestamped like the dashboard events, so one store is the right place for it. And it is one DDL in one place for Raymon to run.
data_store.launchops_chat_memory: MIXED CASE, and out of scope. It is used by the Postgres Chat Memory node in the text agent. Do not rename it, do not touch it, do not join to it. The Postgres account credential is used for nothing in this build.
data_store.access_pattern: PostgREST via the Supabase account f1 credential, through the n8n-nodes-base.supabase node (Resource: Table) or, if those operations are unavailable on this instance, via n8n-nodes-base.httpRequest against the Supabase REST endpoint. Both carry JSON. Neither carries SQL.
data_store.injection_rule: Free text - contact_name, email, company_name, quote_rows_text, total_display, summary_text, price_ledger, services - travels ONLY in a request body. The only values in a URL filter are idempotency_key and contact_id, each regex-validated immediately before use: /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/ for the sha256 digest and /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/ for the contact id. A character set restricted to hex digits, or to alphanumerics plus underscore and hyphen, cannot express a filter, a quote, a semicolon or a comment marker, so the filter path is injection-free by construction rather than by escaping.
data_store.required_service_role_note: The atomic claim needs a service-role key for the Prefer header. An anon key cannot guarantee it. This is a build-blocking open question (Q30).
data_store.attempt_column: REAL COLUMN, not null, default 1, incremented by the reclaim path. The retry cap counts it. An earlier draft used attempt in the idempotency key while the DDL had no such column, so the cap had nothing to count and could not work.
data_store.status_pending_note: pending is the write-ahead in-flight state and is what makes a double-send impossible. A crash between the claim and the send leaves a visible pending row rather than a silent gap, and rather than a claim that pretends an email went out.

quote_document.title: TBD
quote_document.title_note: The business is solar. The old document title was a marketing-agency Service Quote and must not survive.
quote_document.subtitle: TBD
quote_document.date_format_note: Confirm with Raymon. The old document used new Date().toLocaleDateString(), which is locale-dependent and therefore not reproducible between a developer machine and production. Use an explicit format.
quote_document.table_columns_note: The old marketing columns (Monthly Price / One-Time Price) do not fit a solar quote and must not be carried over. Confirm the final column set with Raymon.
quote_document.terms_line_note: For example, prices subject to a site survey. If the quote is an estimate rather than a fixed price, this line is not optional.
quote_document.chat_format: plain text, no markdown, no bullets, no bold, no tables, no HTML, each price in its own message
quote_document.chat_format_note: Matches the live persona's existing output rules so the quote reads like the rest of Amy's messages.
quote_document.all_values_from_catalog: Every value printed on a document or in an email comes from catalog document_defaults. Any "TBD" there that is needed for the output aborts the run with blocked_tbd and sends nothing. Nothing is typed into a node.

dashboard.deployment_url_note: Solar London has no confirmed dashboard deployment. The quote sub-workflow posts an outcome event only once a real URL exists. If there is none, the event node is not created, the graph terminates at each Return node, and the roadmap stage is recorded as SKIPPED with the reason. That is a complete, working state.
dashboard.event_node_note: ONE node, the target of all nine Return nodes, so it cannot be forgotten on a branch. An earlier draft emitted nothing for a blocked or failed quote, which made a lost quote invisible.
dashboard.envelope_note: Canonical and non-negotiable per AGENTS.md section 7. client_id is the GHL contact_id. Both event types are ADDITIVE to the four canonical types and replace none of them. Conversion rate is still booking_made divided by conversations. payload.meta.sample is NEVER set - this is real data only.

kpi_note: A quote_generated KPI card is NOT in scope for the first build. The standard dashboard renders the four canonical KPIs, and a fifth is a separate, separately-approved piece of work. The quote events land in Supabase and are queryable regardless.
open_questions: See clients/solar-london/build-spec/quote-integration-spec.md section 16. Twenty-five questions, numbered 1-25: nine about pricing, four about the catalog, seven business facts that are print-blocking, two policy values, and three with documented defaults. Separately, three STAGE-GATE questions are numbered Q28, Q29 and Q30 - they are NOT questions 28-30 of the 1-25 list, which stops at 25. Of those, TWO are hard build-blocking with no default: Q29 the sending Gmail account, and Q30 whether the Supabase credential holds a service-role key. The third, Q28 the dashboard URL, is stage-gated only: unanswered, S8 is recorded as skipped and the build is complete without it. NO PRICING QUESTION IS BLOCKING - the system ships and is fully testable with every price at "TBD".

verification_commands.check_1_exit_codes: 0 = all pass. 1 = at least one failure, OR the file was not found. 2 = invoked with fewer than two arguments, so nothing was checked at all. Exit 2 is not a pass.
verification_commands.check_1_must_not_glob: PowerShell does not expand a wildcard for a native executable. clients/solar-london/pdfs/*.pdf is passed through literally, the script reports 'file not found', and it exits 1 on a correct file. Always resolve the path in the shell first.
verification_commands.check_1_must_be_pdf: The script is PDF-only. The v1 quote output is an HTML email, so it must be rendered to a PDF repo-side first. The pdf skill at .opencode/.agents/skills/pdf does this. The n8n instance has no access to this repo and no Python in its container, so the skill CANNOT be called from inside a workflow - do not spec it as if it can.
verification_commands.both_required: Check 1 is necessary and NOT sufficient - it passes the old wrong-business copy. Check 2 is derived from the catalog and the workflow export and is what actually catches wrong-business content and a number that did not come from the catalog. A stage is blocked unless BOTH exit 0.
verification_commands.scratch_directory: clients/solar-london/build-spec/render/ is a verification scratch target, not a document store. Its contents are transient and are not committed.
verification_commands.notion_rule: Client documents live in Notion, never in repo folders. There is no clients/solar-london/documents/ folder and this build does not create one. Nothing is filed on the default path - open question 25 in the spec defaults to do-not-file, so a generated quote is NOT uploaded to Notion until Raymon says otherwise. If he does, use scripts/notion-upload-document.mjs with Notion API version 2022-06-28 - never 2025-09-03, which silently drops the schema and yields Name-only databases.

verification_stage_gate: Roadmap stage S1 cannot complete until BOTH checks exit 0. Rendered at S1 with every price still "TBD", so the rendered artifact is the ABORT path output: no numbers, no placeholders, no foreign business. The fact-sheet guard is expected to pass on it, and check 2's catalog-subset check is what proves the right business is on the page.
